money.note: Individuals gave $785,439; PAC money $1,005,574; candidate's own money $0. Percentages describe itemized individual gifts, which the FEC has processed through about July 2026.

cands.bio: Democrat and IBEW electrician who rose to assistant business manager of Local 351 and served 16 years as president of the Southern New Jersey AFL-CIO Central Labor Council. He served in the NJ Assembly (2010) and NJ Senate (2010-2014). He has represented NJ-1 in the U.S. House since November 2014.

controversies.text: Federal records show $27,900 from AIPAC's PAC since 2021; $130,572 from individuals passed through that PAC in 2025-26; 1 trip paid for by the American Israel Education Foundation, AIPAC's affiliate.
This Congress, Norcross missed 95 of 676 House votes (14.1%) through Sept. 16, 2026, including 52 in a row from April 7 to May 22, 2025, after he was hospitalized with a serious illness.

endorsements.text: 2026 endorsements listed by Ballotpedia include New Jersey Citizen Action and Humane World Action Fund.

cands.gaps: We found no documented statements or actions by Norcross on data centers, new development, land or housing purchases by institutional or foreign buyers, school choice or teacher pay, or on homestead property tax relief in Congress. His birth and upbringing are documented, so there is no move-to-New Jersey date. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate surveys. The Ballotpedia page was cut off partway through its list of key votes, so we did not read the remainder. His 2016 and 2013 campaign themes come from Ballotpedia's quotation of older campaign sites, not from pages we read directly. His current campaign site does not address data centers, homestead taxes, immigration enforcement, or guns.

votes.what: The 2025 reconciliation law: extends the 2017 tax cuts, adds new tax breaks, cuts Medicaid and food-assistance spending, and raises defense and border spending and the debt limit.

votes.what: Streamlines coordination among federal agencies delivering disaster aid (hurricane/flood recovery).
Requires federal detention of undocumented immigrants charged with theft, burglary or assault of a police officer, and lets states sue over immigration enforcement.

cands.name: Damon Galdo

top: INSTALLS SHADES, DRAPES, AND BLINDS · Egg Harbor Township, NJ
money.note: Individuals gave $15,545; PAC money $0; candidate's own money $100. Percentages describe itemized individual gifts, which the FEC has processed through about July 2026.

cands.bio: Republican candidate for New Jersey's 1st Congressional District in 2026. Works as a construction superintendent and former carpenter foreman, describes himself as a union carpenter and small business owner, and started the Americas Pulse Network and Jersey Sure podcast. Has not held public office.
cands.gaps: We found no record of Damon Galdo holding public office, so there is no voting or legislative record to report. We could not find where he grew up, when he moved to New Jersey, or how long he has lived in West Deptford. We found no stated positions from him on data centers, development, homestead property taxes, gun laws, abortion, school choice or teacher pay, and no stated position on limiting institutional or foreign buyers of homes and land. Ballotpedia found no endorsements for him in 2026, and we found no documented controversies or foreign ties.

score.why: Raised $16.2k, under $50,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.
score.why_money: Raised $16.2k, under $50,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Carpenter foreman and construction superintendent, described as a small business owner, who started a media network and podcast. He has run for Congress in 2022, 2024 and 2026 and has never held elected or appointed office.
qual.why: His career is real-world trades and business work, but he has no legislative, executive, legal or policy-staff experience, which puts him in the low range for a lawmaking job in Washington.
qual.label: His career is real-world trades and business work, but he has no legislative, executive, legal or policy-staff experience, which puts him in the low range for a lawmaking job in Washington.

workers-first.evidence: Says he supports secure borders, enforcing existing immigration laws, and stronger cooperation between federal and local law enforcement. His 2024 campaign site also said he would propose a ban on sanctuary policies and end DACA and catch-and-release.

back-police-order.evidence: Says he will always support law enforcement officers and wants stronger penalties for violent criminals and drug traffickers.
